title: Algebraization and etale descent of a coherent log ideal
statement:
Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a fine log scheme and $\mathcal I\subset M$ a nonempty coherent log ideal [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum]; fine means etale-locally charted by finitely generated integral commutative monoids, with no saturation requirement. On the small etale site form the ideal sheaf generated by $\alpha(\mathcal I)$. There is a unique quasi-coherent ideal $K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ whose extension to that site is this image ideal. It is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. For every strict etale affine chart $u:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ with monoid chart $P\to A$ and finite nonempty $E\subset P$ generating $\mathcal I$, one has
$$u^*K=\widetilde{(\alpha(e):e\in E)}\subseteq\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}.$$
The chart ideals together with their inclusions into the structure sheaf form the canonical effective descent datum for $K$. This description, including the inclusion and image-ideal equality, commutes with strict etale base change. Here strict means that the source log structure is associated to the inverse image of the target prelog structure.

proof.text: Apply the chart formula theorem to K. Construct each overlap isomorphism by transporting the equality (K.comap u_a).comap f = K.comap V.hom = (K.comap u_b).comap g. Its composite into the structure sheaf is the same ideal inclusion. Cancellation against that mono proves diagonal identity, cocycle and uniqueness. No covering or affineness assumption is needed for this equality construction.

proof.text: For each étale map apply the flat ideal tensor-pullback comparison and turn its isomorphic factor into an isomorphism. Cancellation against the ideal inclusion gives uniqueness with the specified normalization.

proof.text: For a strict étale log map, use the restriction theorem to get source fineness, coherence, image algebraization for K.comap and the equality of image sections. Apply the existence theorem on the source to obtain L. Its uniqueness identifies K.comap with L, transferring finite type. The same uniqueness proves uniqueness for K.comap. Apply the chart formula to K.comap, repeat the overlap equality construction, and apply the flat tensor comparison to the base map.

No new nodes; statement unchanged; the three added stmt_deps (etale association, module pullback, tilde) are notions the statement uses. Source checked: ILO Travaux de Gabber VIII 3.3.7 (PDF p.113, log ideals on fine log schemes via coherent charts) and 3.4.2 (PDF p.116, J=α(I)O_X). Neither the log-regular convention of 3.4.1 nor the bijection of 3.4.3 is imported. Step 1 (elementary): local e·m membership gives J|_U = image of O^E→O; correct. Step 2: quasi-coherent image plus affine sections, then the tilde counit with naturality, gives L_U = Ĩ_E. C1 gap: the epimorphism O^E↠L_U was transported by exactness alone, but the exactness node covers only short exact sequences of quasi-coherent modules and kernel quasi-coherence is not cited. FIX: step 2 now cites lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom (association = ε^*, a colimit-preserving left adjoint with ε^*O = O_et), and exactness is used only on 0→L_U→O_U→O_U/L_U→0 for the monomorphism. proof_deps is unchanged. Step 3: J is site-quasi-coherent by locality; the Zariski/étale equivalence and its inverse (restriction, identity on open sections) give K ⊆ O_X with uniqueness; finite type via the exact/finiteness comparison with no Noetherian hypothesis; coherence not claimed. Step 4: the natural restriction comparison plus full faithfulness gives u^*K = Ĩ_E as ideals; cocycles follow by cancelling against the injection; no affine overlaps assumed. Step 5: strict étale Y is an object of X_et; the generators pull back, so f^*K = K_Y with its inclusion. Small cases checked: unit ideal, α(e)=0, a generator becoming a unit, empty X, a non-saturated monoid. lean.statement: theorem logIdeal_algebraization_descent {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : EtaleLogStructure X) (hM : M.IsFine) (I : M.IdealFamily) (hI : M.IsNonemptyFineCoherentIdeal I) : ∃ K : X.IdealSheafData, Scheme.Modules.IsQuasiCoherentFiniteType K.toModules ∧ M.IsImageIdealAlgebraization I K ∧ (∀ L : X.IdealSheafData, M.IsImageIdealAlgebraization I L → L = K) ∧ M.HasImageIdealChartFormula I K ∧ HasCanonicalEtaleIdealDescent.{u, v} K ∧ (∀ W : X.Etale, ∃! e : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback W.hom).obj K.toModules ≅ (K.comap W.hom).toModules, e.hom ≫ (K.comap W.hom).toModulesι = logIdealTensorInclusion K W.hom) ∧ ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (N : EtaleLogStructure Y) (f : EtaleLogMap N M), f.IsStrictEtale → N.IsFine ∧ N.IsNonemptyFineCoherentIdeal (f.pullbackIdeal I) ∧ Scheme.Modules.IsQuasiCoherentFiniteType (K.comap f.base).toModules ∧ N.IsImageIdealAlgebraization (f.pullbackIdeal I) (K.comap f.base) ∧ (∀ L : Y.IdealSheafData, N.IsImageIdealAlgebraization (f.pullbackIdeal I) L → L = K.comap f.base) ∧ N.HasImageIdealChartFormula (f.pullbackIdeal I) (K.comap f.base) ∧ HasCanonicalEtaleIdealDescent.{u, v} (K.comap f.base) ∧ (∀ (hf : Etale f.base) (V : Y.Etale), N.imageIdealSections (f.pullbackIdeal I) V = M.imageIdealSections I (@Scheme.Etale.mk X V.left (V.hom ≫ f.base) (by have := hf infer_instance))) ∧ (∃! e : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f.base).obj K.toModules ≅ (K.comap f.base).toModules, e.hom ≫ (K.comap f.base).toModulesι = logIdealTensorInclusion K f.base)
